instagram_caption:
A whole period is usually just 6 to 8 teaspoons of blood 🥄

It looks like more because period fluid isn't only blood. Each month the womb builds a new lining, and if there's no pregnancy it sheds, so the flow is blood plus that lining plus mucus. Doctors call a period heavy at about 80 ml (16 teaspoons) or more.

See a doctor if you need a new pad every hour or two, or your period lasts more than 7 days.

Sources: nidirect (NHS info for Northern Ireland), Cleveland Clinic, EBSCO Research Starters.
